To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) low self esteem was associated with the use of Facebook to simulate social relations and with daily hours spent on Facebook, (2) the tendency towards social comparison was an antecedent of the use of Facebook, and (3) the tendency towards simulation was an antecedents of the use of the social network.

a) the tendency toward social comparison on Facebook mediates the relation between low self esteem, and the amount of hours spent on Facebook and the simulation modality of Facebook use; b) for females high self esteem is directly related to social interaction and indirectly related to simulation, and low self esteem is indirectly related to the use of social interaction; c) the dimension of social comparisons on Facebook is more relevant for females than for male students.
low self esteem, social comparison orientation and gender have a significant impact on Facebook use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of self esteem and social comparison in the adoption of Facebook use and with the different modalities in which Facebook is used.
the role of social comparison in the use of Facebook and its relation with low self esteem.
the relationship between self-esteem and Facebook use, and the role of social comparison in this relationship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

self esteem, social comparison, and gender should all be considered when studying the relation between self esteem and Facebook use, and when designing interventions to promote positive use of this social networking site.
social comparison plays a role in the relationship between self-esteem and Facebook use, but this role depends upon the type of use considered and the sex of the users.
the relation between low self esteem (and, in a different way, high self esteem) and Facebook use is mediated by social comparison orientation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social comparison is a crucial variable to understand the use of social networking sites and the role of self esteem in this regard.
the use of Facebook can have both positive and negative effects on self esteem, depending on gender and the specific use of the social network.
the tendency toward social comparison is a relevant mediator between self esteem and Facebook use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Facebook is influenced by different individual traits and that the same traits may have different effects depending on the specific behaviour under investigation.
the use of Facebook may be affected by the tendency to engage in social comparison, which is a trait related to self esteem.
self esteem and social comparison are important predictors of different behaviours enacted on Facebook.
